study: Mixed single-edge and two-edge support proposals
status: Exploratory validation only; no default-method promotion
observations: Cora seed 42: mixed search improves mean binary sufficiency from 0.95 to 1.0 at all three budgets, with unchanged necessity.
Citeseer seed 43: mixed search reduces mean binary necessity from 0.30 to 0.25 at budget 10, with unchanged sufficiency.
The other two runs have unchanged mean binary necessity and sufficiency relative to single-edge gradient search at all budgets.
Mixed coarse-grouped and mixed ungrouped search have identical mean binary metrics in all twelve dataset-seed-budget settings; this does not imply identical supports or continuous metrics.
limitations: Validation queries have informed method development; these are not held-out test estimates.
Two datasets and two model seeds are insufficient to establish general superiority.
The shared per-step proposal cap does not establish equal total computation or runtime.
Saved-trace auditing is not independent re-execution of every intervention.
Coarsening's independent explanation benefit remains unestablished.
Historical LaTeX numerical results remain unchanged and are not validated by this study.
decision: Preserve all outcomes, retain single-edge default, and require broader validation before selecting a final method or replacing manuscript numbers.
